Prove the validity of the decomposition theorem for polyhedra by showing that
every polyhedron P admits the representation P = {x+c : x ∈X, c ∈C}, for some polytope
X and some polyhedral cone C.
Theorem 1 (Decomposition Theorem). Every polyhedron P ⊆Rn admits a representation
P = {x + c : x ∈X, c ∈C} = X + C
where X is a polytope and C is a polyhedral cone.
• A polyhedron is a set P = {x ∈Rn : Ax ≤b} for some matrix
• A polytope is a bounded polyhedron.
• A polyhedral cone is a set C = {x ∈Rn : Ax ≤0} for some matrix A.
• The recession cone of P is CP = {d ∈Rn : x + λd ∈P for all x ∈P, λ ≥0}.
